definitions.explanation: The act of passing completely through something from one side to the other, whether physically (a bullet, a tunnel) or abstractly (an idea running through a work).

examples.japanese: トンネルが{山|やま}を{貫通|かんつう}した。
examples.english: The tunnel pierced through the mountain.

examples.japanese: {弾丸|だんがん}が{壁|かべ}を{貫通|かんつう}した。
この{道路|どうろ}は{市|し}の{中心部|ちゅうしんぶ}を{南北|なんぼく}に{貫通|かんつう}している。
examples.english: This road runs straight through the city center from north to south.

notes:
Emphasizes passing completely through from one side to the other, not merely entering partway. Used both for physical objects (bullets, tunnels, roads) and abstract concepts (a theme or principle running through something). The する verb form is transitive.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弾丸|だんがん}が{貫通|かんつう}する: a bullet penetrates
- トンネルが{貫通|かんつう}する: a tunnel breaks through
- {貫通|かんつう}{傷|しょう}: through-and-through wound
- {南北|なんぼく}に{貫通|かんつう}する: to run through from north to south

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {突|つ}き{抜|ぬ}ける: to break through, to pierce — more dynamic and forceful
- {浸透|しんとう}: permeation, infiltration — gradual spreading through, not a clean puncture
- {通過|つうか}: passing through — moving through without emphasis on piercing
